sections.what: Tells the test runner where tests live, how to read TypeScript and React code, and how to resolve the @ import shortcut.

summary: Test runner settings for the web app: where tests are found, how TypeScript is read and how the @ import shortcut is resolved.
purpose: Lets the test command run tests for the web code.
why: Likely reason: tests are written in TypeScript and use the @ import shortcut. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Looks for test files ending in test.ts or test.tsx under src, compiles them with ts-jest, and maps the @ shortcut to the src folder.
outputs: Test results printed by the test command.
risks: The test environment is set to node rather than a browser, so tests that use browser features may fail or need a different setting.
debug: If a test reports a cannot-find-module error for an @ import, check the mapping in this file. If no tests run, check the file name pattern.
